raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

When a KV offload lookup hits chunks whose GPU->CPU store is still in flight (`HIT_PENDING`), the scheduler always defers the request until the store completes, even if only a chunk or two are pending. Behind a backlog of serialized stores that wait can reach tens of seconds, which shows up as large `vllm:kv_offload_lookup_async_delay_seconds` observations. Recomputing a handful of tokens would have been far cheaper.

This PR adds a `kv_connector_extra_config` option, `max_recompute_pending_tokens`, that bounds the wait:

- If the run of chunks from the first pending chunk to the end of the hit would gain at most this many tokens (rounded down to whole chunks), the prefix lookup is cut before the first pending chunk. The request loads the ready prefix immediately and recomputes the rest.
- The partial-tail lookup applies the same budget.
- `RETRY` results still defer (the chunk's location is unknown), as do pending chunks inside a sliding-window group's required window.
- Negative values are rejected at spec construction.
- Default is `0`, which keeps the current always-wait behavior, so this is a no-op unless opted in.

The option is documented in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `HIT_PENDING offload recompute` and `max_recompute_pending_tokens`. The closest is #53087, which is complementary rather than overlapping: it adds a wall-clock deadline (`hit_pending_timeout_s`) inside `TieringOffloadingManager` for *stalled* primary-tier writes. This PR is a token-budget decision in the connector scheduler that applies to all offloading specs and avoids the wait up front when the pending run is small, rather than timing out after the fact.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
```

New tests:

- `test_recompute_budget_decides_whether_pending_chunks_are_awaited` (end-to-end through the request runner): with chunks `[HIT, HIT_PENDING, HIT]`, a budget covering the pending run loads the ready first chunk and records no async lookup delay; a smaller budget defers as before.
- `_maximal_prefix_lookup` unit cases: short pending run is cut before the first pending chunk, a run one chunk over budget defers, a leading pending chunk within budget is a miss, and `RETRY` defers regardless of budget.
- `test_negative_recompute_budget_is_rejected`.

## Test Result

```text
318 passed, 14 warnings in 106.53s (0:01:46)
```

No model eval or serving benchmark was run: the default (`0`) leaves lookup behavior unchanged, and with the option enabled the request only recomputes tokens it would otherwise have loaded, so outputs are unaffected.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @robertgshaw2-redhat . LGTM in general.
Got 2 points from Claude (have not verified):

1. Split RETRY out of pending in the partial-tail loop (scheduler.py:1032). Right now boundary_pending is set by both HIT_PENDING and RETRY, so any non-zero budget makes RETRY stop deferring — contradicting your own doc row. Keep two flags; gate only the pending one.

2. Gate on the highest awaitable pending boundary, not max_boundary (scheduler.py:1050). max_boundary - complete_boundary is the best case at the top candidate, but the pending boundary can be far lower, so the feature under-triggers exactly where it's meant to fire. Also skip boundaries that had a MISS in another group — those can never become hits, so deferring for them buys nothing.

+| `max_recompute_pending_tokens` | no | `0` | both | A lookup that hits chunks whose offload is still in flight (`HIT_PENDING`) normally waits for them. If waiting would gain at most this many tokens (rounded down to whole chunks), the request instead loads the ready prefix and recomputes the rest. Pending chunks inside a sliding-window group's required window and uncertain (`RETRY`) results still wait. `0` always waits. |
 | `self_describing_kv_events` | no | `false` | both | Opt-in. When `true` *and* KV cache events are enabled (`--kv-events-config` with `enable_kv_cache_events`), the connector emits self-describing block-granular `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` payloads (constituent block hashes, whole-chunk `token_ids`, per-block `block_size`, parent hash, LoRA + group/cache-spec metadata) instead of the placeholder fallback, so external KV-event consumers can index offloaded blocks. Inert unless events are enabled. With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a CPU promotion is self-describing when a local request observes its primary-tier `HIT` before event translation; otherwise its stored event may retain the placeholder, while a later `HIT` can backfill metadata for removal. Pending-removal/re-promotion races and externally initiated promotions may also produce placeholders, and consumers must ignore removals for unknown hashes. Partial recurrent tails emit the hash-aligned portion from the physical block start through the tail boundary. Other sliding-window/SSM chunks keep the placeholder fallback. In chunk mode (`block_size` > GPU block size, or `blocks_per_chunk` > 1), overlapping chunks re-announce shared per-block hashes, so consumers must reference-count (deduplicate) repeated store/remove announcements. |
 | `spec_module_path` | no | — | both | Python import path for a custom `OffloadingSpec` not in the built-in registry. Required only when `spec_name` is not built-in (advanced). |
